literal: If [I] blink, [his] hiding I know; just for that, 'stranger' says this town.
translation: I know that if I blink, my lover who lives in my eyes will be hidden from me; yet, just because I do not blink to avoid this, the people of this town call him an unkind stranger.
modern: நான் கண் இமைத்தால் என் கண்ணுக்குள் இருக்கும் காதலர் மறைந்துவிடுவார் என்பதை நான் அறிவேன்; அவ்வாறு இமைக்காமல் இருப்பதைக் கண்டு, இந்த ஊர் மக்கள் அவரை அன்பில்லாதவர் என்று தூற்றுகின்றனர்.
explanation: The heroine explains that her lover is always present inside her eyes. She avoids blinking because she knows that even a momentary blink would hide him from her sight. However, the ignorant villagers do not understand this sweet secret; seeing her unblinking, tearful, or strained eyes, they gossip and call her lover an unsympathetic stranger who does not care for her. The word 'karappākku' refers to the hiding of her lover, and 'ētilar' highlights the town's lack of understanding, as they mistake her loving vigilance for distress caused by an uncaring partner.
